Q: Multiple case expressions result in rows being duplicated A:

Presuming the query is written correctly, you could just need GROUP BY ....

A standard approach to this situation is to use an aggregate function with those many CASE expressions, usually MAX() or MIN(). Then add a GROUP BY on JK_UniqueConsignRef and any other non-aggregated columns.

  MAX(CASE WHEN XV_Name = 'Master Booking' THEN XV_DATA END) AS MasterBooking,                                                                                     
  MAX(CASE WHEN XV_Name = 'Planning Note'  THEN XV_DATA END) AS PlanningNote,                                                                                      
  -- etc.

WHERE 
  -- ... 

GROUP BY 
  JK_UniqueConsignRef, 
  -- etc.

Caveats/notes:

If each ConsolID has at most one row per XV_Name, MAX() then just picks a single value. this pattern can be called conditional aggregation, or pivot.

It can silently lose data: if a ConsolID can have multiple rows with the same XV_Name, MAX() picks one arbitrarily. If that's possible in your data, decide intentionally what to do in that case. For example, concatenate or add a tiebreaker to a subquery that pre-filters to one row per name. Window functions ROW_NUMBER(), RANK(), DENSE_RANK() can be used here if your RDBMS supports them.

Since you have so many columns, a cleaner and more sustainable alternative is a subquery or CTE that pre-pivots: join to just the pivoted XV_Name/XV_DATA rows before the main SELECT. This keeps the main query cleaner and the pivot logic isolated.

Q: How to use concat A:

The main reason your query is crashing is likely because you're using the word SET more than once. In BigQuery, you only write SET once and then list your columns with a comma in between.

Use the NULLIF function because it’s the fastest way to tell the database, "if this is a zero, kill it and make it null." You also need a WHERE clause at the bottom so you don't waste money processing rows that are already clean. Check your schema to be sure the columns aren't locked as "Required", or the nulls won't stick. Finally, put those backticks around your table name if your project ID has any weird characters like dashes.

Use the code below:

UPDATE `project.dataset.table`  
SET wind_speed = NULLIF(wind_speed, 0),  
    visibility = NULLIF(visibility, 0)  
WHERE wind_speed = 0 OR visibility = 0;

Q: undefined variable on codeigniter A:

We're missing some details to quickly solve this one: namely, how is giris.php called, exactly? Without those details I can only give a general answer.

This error means that you are trying to access data in your template file that you haven't passed to the templating system. For instance, in your controller (Slider.php) you pass data off to the templates here:

$this->load->view('slider_view' ,$data);

The $data is the important part: codeigniter takes every entry in that array and creates a variable in the template system whos name corresponds to the name of each key. Therefore, foreach( $manset as $row ) works because $data has a key named manset that has each row in it. You can see that in giris.php you are specifically not sending any data to the template:

$this->load->view('slider_view');

Notice the lack of a second parameter. Of course your file structure implies that giris.php is itself a view file, which means that whatever controller method that called giris.php needs to be the one sending data out to the view. So generally, that is the answer: whatever controller is ultimately calling giris.php needs to be sending the slider information out to the templating system, but isn't. Without more details on how giris.php is actually called, that is as specific as I can get.

Q: Best SQL Function for Text Filtering A:

I would have say LIKE but I guess your need it's not that simple.

Maybe you want to apply a full text search? Not only on a specific column but on your whole table whatever the column?

If it's the case, you can use the SEARCH.

CREATE SEARCH INDEX search_index ON mydataset.sports(ALL COLUMNS)

SELECT * FROM `mydataset.sports`
WHERE SEARCH(sports, 'soccer');

It would even find Soccer or SOCCER
